newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Blue-chip buying buoys Singapore shares at open.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip buying buoys Singapore shares at open.

text.p: Singapore shares edged higher at the open on buying of select blue chip counters on Wednesday, but dealers said overall activity remained quiet.

They said the Dow's 23-point overnight surge to an all-time record close above 5,900 points provided some support, but the market was awaiting the release of U.S. jobs data on Friday for further indications of the U.S. interest rate outlook.
At 0200 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 2.30 points at 2,173.99 points. Market volume was 14.63 million shares with gainers outpacing losers by 79 to 34.
Singapore Telecom was active with several block trades at Singapore $3.20 (US$2.27).
"The downside looks pretty limited. I wouldn't be surprised if it goes back to S$3.30," said a dealer with a local house.

Keppel Corp and Jurong Shipyard rebounded from yesterday's losses and were each up S$0.20 to S$10.70 and S$6.85 respectively while the foreign tranches of Singapore Press Holdings and DBS Bank shed S$0.20 and S$0.10 each to S$25.10 and S$17.20.
Van Der Horst added S$0.20 to S$5.60 after it confirmed a S$204 million joint venture project on Monday to build and operate a toll road in Indonesia.
